applications: Control interface for compatible WyreStorm systems

recommendedWhen: Control interface for compatible WyreStorm systems

salesLanguage.headline: NETWORKHDTOUCHTM: gives users a simpler way to run the room
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the customer needs buttons, touch control, protocol conversion or a cleaner way to trigger room behaviour.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It helps hide technical complexity from everyday users.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Meeting rooms, classrooms, AV racks and controlled presentation spaces.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Talk about the action the user wants, not the protocol.
talkTrack: It turns technical commands into practical room actions.
It should be tied to a clear user workflow or control requirement.
discoveryPrompts: Who controls the room?
What actions should be one-touch?
Which devices need control: display, switcher, source, lift, lighting or audio?
positioningNotes: Use when control simplicity or integration is part of the requirement.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not add control hardware unless there is a clear control task.
marketApplications: Control interface for compatible WyreStorm systems

endUser.headline: NETWORKHDTOUCHTM: gives users a simpler way to run the room
endUser.pitch: Use this when the customer needs buttons, touch control, protocol conversion or a cleaner way to trigger room behaviour.
endUser.value: It helps hide technical complexity from everyday users.
talkTrack: Talk about the action the user wants, not the protocol.

discoveryPrompts: What do users need to do when they walk into the room?
What would make the room feel easier or more reliable for everyday use?

What actions should be one-touch?
positioningNotes: Keep the language about outcomes and the user experience before talking about ports.
Use when control simplicity or integration is part of the requirement.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not add control hardware unless there is a clear control task.

systemIntegrator.label: SI / installer
systemIntegrator.headline: NETWORKHDTOUCHTM: deployment and commissioning view
systemIntegrator.pitch: Use this view when the installer needs to confirm what each button, touch action or control command actually triggers in the room.
systemIntegrator.value: Turns the sales conversation into practical install checks: location, cabling, signal direction, dependencies, control and commissioning risk.
talkTrack: Check the practical signal path around IP, NetworkHD AV over IP before finalising the design.
Confirm what connects locally, what leaves the room, and which accessories or endpoints are required.
Check USB class, power method, control path and firmware notes before treating the product as a like-for-like substitute.
discoveryPrompts: Where will the product physically live: table, wall, display, rack, lectern or network closet?
What cable type, distance and route are available between each endpoint?
Which products, receivers, USB devices, controllers or network switches must be present for this to work?
Who controls the room?
What actions should be one-touch?
positioningNotes: Good installer language should make dependencies visible before a quote is issued.
Call out install risk early when the product depends on USB bandwidth, network design, endpoint pairing or control integration.
Use when control simplicity or integration is part of the requirement.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not imply it is plug-and-play where cable distance, USB class, endpoint compatibility, network design or control programming still needs validation.
Do not add control hardware unless there is a clear control task.

consultant.label: Consultant / technical
consultant.headline: NETWORKHDTOUCHTM: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to decide whether the control requirement is real, what user actions matter, and whether this product simplifies or complicates the room.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.
discoveryPrompts: Is this requirement driven by user experience, source/display routing, distance, USB, collaboration, network distribution, processing or control?
What would make this product the wrong choice even if it technically works?
Is the system expected to grow, change rooms, add endpoints, record, stream or integrate with a wider AV platform?
Who controls the room?
What actions should be one-touch?
positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.
Be explicit when the product is technically possible but unlikely to be the most natural choice.
Use when control simplicity or integration is part of the requirement.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not let a feature match override the real application, architecture or operational requirement.
Do not add control hardware unless there is a clear control task.

governedSpecification.productType: Free iPad & Android Control App for NetworkHD 100, 200, 400, 500 and 600 Series

evidence.excerpt: Free iPad & Android Control App for NetworkHD 100, 200, 400, 500 and 600 Series

evidence.note: Confirmed in the 2026-09-30 structured review pass directed by Steve Goodwin. Spec-critical fields cross-checked field-by-field against the live official WyreStorm product page (canonical store captures with officialPageStatus 200, or the profile's own live evidence page where the store capture was not a live page).

dependencies: A NetworkHD encoder/decoder endpoint (100, 200, 400, 500 or 600 series) for the system the app controls
NetworkHD controller (NHD-CTL-PRO-V2) on the same managed 1GbE network for route and device control

sourceCatalog.lifecycleReason: Duplicate catalogue record for the same free NetworkHD companion control app already represented by NHD-TOUCH (which WyreStorm's own 2026 discontinued business list also lists as discontinued, likely superseded by the newer Companion Control App). Consolidated onto NHD-TOUCH rather than keeping two records for one product.
